page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized server instance within the n2d family. It features 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, running on an x86_64 architecture. The processing power is delivered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 CPU, which consists of 1 physical core and 2 threads. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES and VAES cryptography, and SHA_NI. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 25%. However, its multi-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show poor to weak results, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 126.54 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 22.01 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while multi-core workloads, including compiling software, ray tracing, and database operations, score in the bottom 10% to 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, the n2d-highmem-2 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense parallel processing. It is suitable for lightweight memory-intensive applications, basic caching layers, single-threaded data processing, and small-scale web serving. It is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks, multi-threaded compiling, or high-throughput database operations due to its limited physical core count and lower multi-core benchmark scores.
